item.title: Boost.Asio Strands Explained Thread Safety and Asynchronous Operations
item.description:
“Boost.Asio Strands Explained Thread Safety and Asynchronous Operations”

When working with asynchronous operations in C++ using Boost.Asio, managing thread safety is crucial. This is particularly evident when dealing with operations on shared resources like sockets. Boost.Asio’s strand object provides a mechanism to serialize handler invocations, preventing race conditions and ensuring predictable execution flow.

Understanding the Problem: Concurrent Access

Consider a typical asynchronous network application. Operations like async_receive and async_write initiate handlers that are called when an I/O event occurs. If multiple threads are running the io_context’s run() method, these handlers could potentially execute concurrently. This poses a risk if the handlers access shared data or the underlying socket object in an unsafe manner.
